name: Ziz Palm Grove
hero_subtitle: Green palm corridors of the Ziz valley framing the approaches to Erfoud.

overview.title: Palms at the desert edge
overview.p1: The Ziz valley threads a ribbon of date palms through an arid landscape. Around Erfoud the contrast is clear: green corridors, irrigation and villages tied to the grove.
overview.p2: Short stops along the road and a walk at the palm edge already show why the Tafilalet was a historic corridor between mountains and Sahara.
overview.p3: Bring water and a hat. Shade under the palms is real; open stretches are harsh at midday.

1.title: Cooler
1.desc: Best for walking markets and photos.

1.title: Access
1.desc: Most visitors see the palms from the main roads into Erfoud or a short taxi detour.

2.title: Respect the grove
2.desc: Paths cross private plots. Stay on public tracks and ask before entering enclosures.

3.title: Combine
3.desc: Palm edges and Erfoud centre work well on the same day without rushing.

gyg.title: From Erfoud
gyg.subtitle: Desert day trips use desert roads.

q1.question: Is it a formal park?
q1.answer: No. It is a living agricultural landscape of date palms along the Ziz.

q2.question: Can I walk inside?
q2.answer: Along public edges and tracks, yes. Avoid private plots without permission.

q3.question: How long?
q3.answer: 45 to 90 minutes for viewpoints and a short walk.

q4.question: Best season?
q4.answer: October to April for milder heat; in summer go early or late only.

q5.question: Why does it matter?
q5.answer: The Ziz corridor supported caravan routes and still feeds Tafilalet towns with dates and shade.
